site.name: Itqan
site.strapline: The jobs that fit you, and a path to the ones you want.
site.description: Itqan reads your record, CV and certificates against real openings, shows you the jobs you fit today with the reason for each, and the shortest path to the role you want next. Free, in Arabic and English.

chat.greeting: Hello. I am Hud. Ask me about Itqan: what it does, what it does not do, and what happens to your documents.
chat.noMatchBody: I do not have a ready answer for that. I can answer questions about Itqan itself: what it does, what it costs, and what happens to your documents. Anything about you specifically I cannot answer until I have read your record, and that starts with a free account.

It reads them, checks what you have against openings that are genuinely live in the Gulf, then shows you the jobs you fit today and the reason behind each one. After that it lays out the shortest path to the role you want next, in real courses.

forks.a: Yes. The gap, the full path, the job matches and the advisor are free and stay free. Nobody pays to get hired. There is no card to enter and no plan to pick.

forks.keywords: transcript document documents upload privacy data record certificate store stored delete safe security
forks.a: It gets read so your courses can be matched to the skills they actually cover. Before anything moves on from there, the extracted list is put in front of you to check and correct. That screen is where the decision sits, and it is yours rather than ours.

forks.q: My degree is not from Oman. Does that work?
forks.keywords: outside oman abroad foreign international degree university visa sponsor gulf english expat
forks.a: Yes. Itqan is built for Arabic and English equally, and it reads records from outside the Gulf. Where it is unsure about a course it says so and asks you to confirm, rather than guessing.

footer.tagline: An Arabic platform that helps graduates read their own skills clearly.

hero.heading: The jobs that fit you are already out there. Itqan finds them, and shows you why.
hero.sub: Give it your record, your CV and your certificates, and answer a few short questions. Itqan checks all of it against real openings, shows you the ones you fit today, and lays out the shortest path to the role you want next.

problem.heading: The hard part is not you

cards.title: Hours spent applying, nothing back
cards.body: You send application after application and the replies barely come. Most of those roles were never going to fit, but you only find that out after the evening is gone.

cards.title: Every posting looks almost right
cards.body: The title fits. Then one line in the requirements does not, and you cannot tell if it is worth your time. So you apply on a guess, or you close the tab on a guess.

cards.title: You know the goal, not the way in
cards.body: There is a role you are working toward. Between here and there is a short list of things to learn. No one has laid it out for you.

example.why: Your statistics coursework, your data certificate and the reporting you did last year cover four of the five things this role asks for. The fifth is a short course away, and Itqan shows you which one.

cols.body: You are closer to a role than it feels. Itqan shows which ones fit now, and the shortest way to the rest.

items.a: Yes. Everything in Itqan is free. No plans, no trial period, and no payment at any point.

items.q: What do you need from me?
items.a: Your academic record, and if you have them, your CV, resume and certificates. Then a few short questions, up to ten, so Itqan understands what you are aiming for. The more it has, the sharper the fit.

items.q: Do you find real jobs, or just give advice?
items.a: Real openings that exist right now, matched to you, each with the reason it fits. Itqan does not promise you a job. It shows you where you have a real chance and where you do not.

items.q: What if nothing fits me yet?
items.a: Then you get a path. Itqan shows the role you are aiming for, what you already have toward it, and the shortest set of things to learn to get there.

items.q: Do I have to be Omani?
items.a: No. Itqan starts in Oman and reads Arabic and English documents, so graduates across the Gulf can use it.
Yes, at any time. Deleting your account removes everything you gave Itqan and everything built from it.

closing.heading: See the jobs that fit you

hiw.title: How Itqan works
hiw.metaDescription: Four steps from your academic record to skills employers understand. No inflated numbers, no promises.
hiw.intro: Four steps. No magic in any of them.

steps.title: You share your academic record
steps.body: Your transcript is the input. Not a CV, not a form with twenty fields. The document you already have.

steps.title: It reads your courses and you confirm them
steps.body: Itqan shows you every course it read, exactly as it read it. You fix anything wrong and approve the list. Nothing moves forward without your confirmation. This step exists because a result you checked yourself is worth more than a result you were handed.

steps.title: It matches your skills against real openings
steps.body: Every skill it names is matched against openings that actually exist, and every match can be checked against its original source.

steps.title: It shows what is missing and how to close it
steps.body: What you have comes first. Then the gaps, each with a concrete way to close it. A gap is a next step, not a verdict.

proof.title: Proof
proof.metaDescription: A full example of how Itqan translates an academic record, with its current limits stated plainly.
proof.heading: Do not take our word for it
proof.intro: This page shows the reasoning itself, so you can judge it before creating anything.

example.heading: A record, read in full
example.intro: Five courses from an IT graduate record, and what they translate to for employers.

rows.why: Queries, table design and normalisation are the working content of this course. Employers write that as SQL.
The course teaches object oriented design and its projects are built in Java. Both words belong on your profile.
Descriptive statistics, probability and interpreting results: postings call this data analysis.
The course centres on turning what a client needs into a specification. Postings ask for it as requirements gathering.
The record shows the course but not the tools you used in it, so this one is labelled a suggestion until you confirm it.

example.note: An illustrative example. Inside the product, each match links to a live posting with the date it was retrieved.

how.heading: How a match is justified
how.p1: A match is a chain with three links: a course on your record, the skill inside that course, and a posting that asks for that skill. Itqan shows the whole chain every time, under the name why this match.
how.p2: When the chain is strong, the match says so. When any link is weaker, the match is labelled a suggestion for you to confirm. It is never presented as fact.

limits.heading: What Itqan cannot do yet
items: It cannot promise you a job. It shows you where you stand and what closes the distance. The applying is still yours.
It has not published an accuracy figure, because measurement on enough real records is not finished. Publishing a number before that would be a guess.
Some results are suggestions to confirm, not facts. They are labelled.
A transcript is a starting point, not the whole picture of you. Projects, work and character live outside it.
It reads Arabic and English records. Other languages, not yet.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.metaDescription: How Itqan collects, keeps and protects your data.
privacy.heading: How your data is handled
privacy.intro: This page sets the structure of the notice. The legal text itself is written by a lawyer before launch.
privacy.noticeLabel: A lawyer completes this section. Questions to answer:

sections.heading: What is collected
questions: Which fields are required at sign up?
Is the original transcript file kept, or only the extracted text?
What usage data or technical logs are collected?

sections.heading: Why it is collected
questions: What is the lawful basis for each processing purpose? Explicit consent is the only basis available.
Is data used to improve the models? If so, under what consent?

sections.heading: How long it is kept
questions: How long is an inactive account kept?
When are uploaded files permanently deleted?

sections.heading: Who it is shared with
questions: Who are the hosting and processing providers, and where are their servers?
Does data leave Oman, and under what safeguards?

sections.heading: Your rights
questions: How does a user request a copy of their data?
How is consent withdrawn, and what happens after withdrawal?
What is the response time for requests?

sections.heading: Contact the data officer
questions: Who is the data protection officer?
What is the official email and postal address?

about.title: Who we are
about.metaDescription: Why we built Itqan, how it works, and what it does. We show you the distance to the job you want and the shortest way to close it.
about.whyHeading: You know where you want to end up. No one tells you how far that is, or which way to go.
about.whyBody: We started Itqan because that distance should be visible from the start, not discovered after years of applying and being turned down. The hard part was never what you already have. It is what stands between you and where you want to be, and what to do about it.
about.mission: We show you how far you are from the job you want, the shortest way to close that distance, and the real jobs that fit you today.
about.vision: A world where no graduate has to guess their next step.
about.how1Title: We measure against the real market.
about.how1Body: Live Gulf demand, not a generic checklist of what a role is supposed to need.
about.how2Body: Every recommendation carries its reason and a real source you can open. Nothing invented is ever shown to you.
about.how3Body: No employer can buy a place in what you see.
about.what1Body: between you and the role you want.
about.what3Title: Finds the jobs that fit you now,
about.evidenceHeading: We asked graduates and final year students in Oman.
about.evidenceBody: Roughly two thirds had read a job posting and could not tell whether a course they took counted as the skill being asked for. Nearly nine in ten were blocked by postings demanding experience they did not have. Nearly half of those who were rejected could not say why.
about.evidenceQualifier: An early sample, drawn from the graduates we are launching to. We are widening it.
about.whereBody: We are embedded at UTAS, which is both our first pilot and where our survey came from. Our regulator, MTCIT, runs Khuta, which we treat as a distribution channel rather than a competitor. We start in Oman, then Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf.
about.payEyebrow: What you will never pay for
about.payBody: You never pay to get hired. The core is free forever: the gap, the full path, the top job matches and the advisor. The paid tier is for people who already have income, not for you if you are still looking. Employers and universities pay for access to candidates who agreed to it.
about.refuse1: We will not sell a place in your results.
about.refuse2: We will not invent a course or a job that does not exist.
about.refuse3: We will not promise you a job.
about.refuse4: We will not publish an accuracy figure we have not measured.
